stories.headline: Takaichi completes Vietnam summit, arrives in Australia on five-day Indo-Pacific tour
stories.summary: Prime Minister Takaichi visited Hanoi on May 1–3, signing six bilateral agreements with Vietnam and delivering a major keynote speech at Vietnam National University revamping Japan's 'Free and Open Indo-Pacific' strategy with new emphasis on energy security, supply chains, space, and critical minerals. She then departed for Canberra, arriving late May 3 for a three-day visit to mark the 50th anniversary of the Japan-Australia Basic Treaty, with defence, critical minerals, and energy supply (in context of the Strait of Hormuz closure) as headline agenda items.

stories.headline: Takaichi signals renewed push for constitutional revision on Constitution Memorial Day
stories.summary: On May 3, Constitution Memorial Day (the 79th anniversary of Japan's postwar charter taking effect), Prime Minister Takaichi delivered a prerecorded video message to a gathering of revision proponents calling for the constitution to be 'periodically updated' to reflect current security realities—widely read as a renewed push to amend pacifist Article 9. A concurrent poll showed public support for revision holding above 50%.

stories.headline: Japan scraps lethal weapons export ban, inaugurates security document review panel; China condemns shift
stories.summary: The Takaichi Cabinet scrapped long-standing restrictions on lethal weapons exports in late April, allowing sales to 17 partner countries, and the prime minister simultaneously inaugurated an advisory panel to revise Japan's three key security documents. The moves drew reaction from Ukraine (which sees a path to future Japanese arms), India (which welcomed the policy), and China (whose foreign ministry condemned Tokyo's 'militaristic' trajectory).

stories.headline: Japan intervenes in currency markets for first time in two years to prop up yen
stories.summary: Japanese authorities intervened in foreign exchange markets on April 30 to support the yen, its first such action in nearly two years, pushing the dollar down roughly 3% to around 155.5 yen. Japan's top currency diplomat Atsushi Mimura subsequently warned that speculative positions remained evident, signalling readiness to act again; the yen sustained gains through the week.

stories.headline: Bank of Japan holds rates at 0.75% with three dissents, Ueda keeps June hike option open
stories.summary: The Bank of Japan kept its benchmark policy rate unchanged at 0.75% at its April 28 meeting, citing uncertainty from the Middle East conflict, but three of nine board members dissented in favour of a hike—the highest dissent count in recent memory. Governor Kazuo Ueda signalled at his press conference that underlying inflation was approaching 2% and kept the door open to a June move, but declined to give a specific timing signal, sending the yen lower.

stories.headline: Takaichi and foreign minister press Iran directly on Strait of Hormuz passage
stories.summary: Prime Minister Takaichi held phone talks with Iranian President Pezeshkian on April 30, urging Iran to ensure safe passage for all ships through the Strait of Hormuz and calling for swift resumption of US-Iran negotiations. Japan's foreign minister separately urged his Iranian counterpart to show 'flexibility' in the standoff. The Diplomat reported that the ruling LDP had submitted formal policy proposals to Takaichi on how to leverage Japan's existing regional military presence to support safe passage.

stories.headline: State ceremony marks 100th anniversary of start of Showa Era; Emperor Naruhito and Takaichi attend
stories.summary: On April 30 (Showa Day, a national holiday), the Japanese government held a ceremony at Tokyo's Nippon Budokan attended by Emperor Naruhito, Empress Masako, Prime Minister Takaichi, the Upper House president, Lower House speaker, Supreme Court chief justice, and approximately 5,620 others, commemorating the centennial of the Showa Era's start in 1926. Takaichi gave a speech drawing lessons from the era for contemporary Japan.

stories.headline: Takaichi resists calls for energy-saving measures as Middle East supply anxiety grows
stories.summary: With the war in the Middle East disrupting energy supplies, Prime Minister Takaichi took a publicly negative stance on April 28 against urging the Japanese public to limit energy consumption, arguing current supply projections—including naphtha-derived petrochemicals—remain sufficient through year-end. The Japan Times reported public polling showing the majority of Japanese favour conservation measures, putting Takaichi's position at odds with popular sentiment.

stories.headline: Japan LDP delegation meets India's BJP leadership to deepen party-to-party and bilateral ties
stories.summary: A high-level LDP delegation led by policy research council chair Kobayashi Takayuki met BJP National President Nitin Nabin in New Delhi on May 3, discussing expansion of party-to-party links and Indo-Pacific cooperation. India's external affairs ministry separately welcomed Japan's new defence equipment transfer policy as a boost for bilateral security cooperation.

stories.headline: LDP proposes civil penalties for AI companies enabling copyright infringement and deepfakes
stories.summary: Japan's ruling LDP formally called for new civil penalties targeting AI companies whose tools are used to infringe copyright or produce deepfakes, with a draft proposal to strengthen Japan's existing AI Law expected to be submitted to the government as early as May. Coverage appeared on IP and technology law outlets.
